topic: Thread Requirement: Move-Only Construction for Wrappers
explanation: Since `std::thread` objects are resource handles that are non-copyable, they must be treated as move-only types. When constructing an RAII wrapper or container around a `std::thread`, the wrapper’s constructor must accept the thread object as an rvalue reference (`std::thread&&`) and use `std::move` in the member initialization list to transfer ownership safely. Why It Fails: Attempting to pass a `std::thread` by const reference or copy into the wrapper will result in a compilation error because `std::thread` lacks a copy constructor. The move operation ensures the resource handle is transferred cleanly.
code_example:
ThreadRAII(std::thread&& t, DtorAction a)
: action(a), t(std::move(t)) {}
practical_example: A developer attempts to pass a local `std::thread` instance to an RAII manager by value, leading to a compiler error due to the attempted copy. The developer must explicitly cast the local thread variable to an rvalue using `std::move` when calling the constructor, or the constructor must accept the rvalue directly.
